name: apple-calendar-mcp
description: Read and manage macOS Calendar events through EventKit
long_description:
A local MCP server written in Swift that gives Claude access to the Calendar app on this Mac.

There is no network, no account and no API key. iCloud is only the sync engine that fills the local calendar store. The gate is macOS privacy consent, and the grant appears under System Settings → Privacy & Security → Calendars. Full access is required: write-only access cannot read events back, so the server could not confirm what it created.

Plug and play: there is nothing to configure. Every calendar is reachable; the only control over this server is its own per-tool permission switch below.

Every result is bounded. Events and calendars come one page at a time, and a long event one window at a time; when a result does not hold everything, its first lines say how much there is and the exact arguments that return the rest (limit and offset, or character_offset and max_characters). A search takes from_date and to_date, both included, or starts today when given neither. One call looks at no more than 1464 days and says where it stopped and how to continue. A size outside its range is moved to the nearest allowed value, and the result says which one was used; a date that does not exist is refused.

Creating and updating answer with a short receipt, not the whole event. Deleting returns what it removed, once, because nothing can read it afterwards.

Every call is bounded too: one that has not finished after 30 seconds is abandoned and answered with an error that says so.

EventKit cannot invite attendees and cannot create repeating events; both must be done in Calendar.app.

An event can be moved to another calendar, but a recurring one cannot: its calendar belongs to the whole series, and EventKit does not define splitting a series across calendars.

Not affiliated with or endorsed by Apple Inc.

tools.name: calendar_status
tools.description: Reports whether Calendar access is granted and how to grant it, and the sizes results keep to. Reads no events.

tools.name: calendars_list
tools.description: Lists calendars one page at a time, with their accounts and which accept writes; limit and offset reach the rest.

tools.name: calendar_search
tools.description: Finds events one page at a time, oldest first, from today onwards or between from_date and to_date (both included), optionally filtered by text and calendar. A long title, calendar name or location is clipped; notes are left to calendar_get.

tools.name: calendar_get
tools.description: Reads one event's record, including whether it is past, in progress or upcoming, with a page of its attendees. A long record comes one window at a time.

tools.name: create_event
tools.description: Adds an event and answers with a short receipt. Cannot invite attendees or create a repeating series.

tools.name: update_event
tools.description: Changes an event, including one that has already ended, and answers with a short receipt. Can move it to another calendar, unless it is recurring.

tools.name: delete_event
tools.description: Permanently deletes an event, including one that has already ended, and returns what it removed. Requires explicit confirmation.
